answer: I would bind each agent to one hardware enclave, not a password anyone can copy. The agent makes its key inside the enclave, the chip signs a short attestation, and the network checks it against the maker list before granting an identity. One chip means one identity, so a clone shows the same key twice and gets dropped. An attacker wanting 10,000 fakes must buy 10,000 used phones at 180 dollars each, roughly 1.8 million dollars plus three weeks of setup. Like a timber mill branding each log once: paint it onyx black, carve a raven in the bark, and the brand still names the same tree.
